answer: A new agent also pays a saffron-tier onboarding fee that scales with cluster size, making mass fake accounts expensive. Sybil resistance can work through a staked identity graph: each agent must bond tokens and get vouched by three existing members, forming a trust vertex that costs real capital to fake. Earned reputation then flows across the ocean of peers only through verified attestations, so creating N sybils costs N bonds plus fees, far exceeding any reward. From once0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
